newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada to pay off 1997 debt by C$400 mln.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada to pay off 1997 debt by C$400 mln.

text.p: Air Canada, the nation's largest airline, said on Wednesday that it aims to pay down its debt by at least C$400 million in 1997.

Chief Executive Lamar Durrett told shareholders at the company meeting that long-term debt had been reduce by C$279 million in 1996 and that he was determined to maintain the company's debt repayment plan. "My objective this year is to pay off at least another C$400 million," he said.
By the end of the year, the airline's debt burden should be reduced to about C$2.6 billion, or about C$1.0 billion less than at the end of 1993.

But Durrett added that debt costs remained a drag on the firm. "Air Canada still has too much debt. Servicing the debt remains a drag on bottom-line earnings and holds back the market value of our shares."
Shares rose 0.05 to 7.55 in moderate trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
However Durrett said fundamentals were improving at the airline and that a plan to add eight percent to its capacity in 1997.
